## TL;DR

Adjusted first-load skeletons so Mission Control and Stories use a single representative block, kept the named item-count map and Settings row count, and retained the shell-level delay/minimum display timing. Removed the shell cross-fade and its out-of-flow transition treatment so the route replaces the skeleton in normal flow. Cleared loading-state screenshot declarations because the capture verifier rejects pages that are still loading.

## Work and rationale

The final scope followed the accepted release decision: keep the app-shell show delay and minimum visible duration, but leave per-view skeleton gating and additional transition behavior to follow-up work. Mission Control stays a single block, avoiding the earlier six-card shape that looked like a board and could wrap awkwardly. Stories keeps the simple rows shape. Named skeleton counts remain available for the supported kinds, with per-kind tests checking rendered counts; the Settings rows count stays at the representative grouped-list value rather than collapsing to one.

A prior review noted that cross-fading the outgoing skeleton with the incoming route caused both flex children to occupy space and squeeze the page. The later scope decision was to remove the fade entirely. The final App shell therefore switches directly between the loading shell and RouterView, and the route remains in its normal flex layout. Reduced-motion behavior continues to avoid animation.

The declared screenshots targeted loading-state selectors, but the shot tool deliberately rejects any capture with an aria-busy/loading indicator; settled pages do not contain those skeleton selectors either. I cleared the loading screenshots instead of leaving a review plan that fails on missing targets. Component tests provide the structural and count assertions for this accepted scope.

## Approaches tried

The initial shell cross-fade was removed after review found a flex overlap during exit. I then kept the final implementation to an immediate conditional swap, with no leave transition or absolute positioning. Earlier review proposals to gate every per-view skeleton and to expand representative block counts were superseded by the owner’s frozen scope; those changes are assigned to follow-up #1078. The final screenshot plan was cleared to match the no-loading-state-capture decision.

## Challenges and blockers

Remote validation on the first runner hung, so RepoOS retried on a second host. The second run completed successfully. A previous server finalization also encountered an overlapping check while trying to commit the engineering report; this run waited for that check to finish, then ran validation on the current stable tree before writing this draft. No implementation blocker remains.

## Key learnings

A loading-state screenshot is not usable evidence when the capture system treats aria-busy as a failed shot. Skeleton structure and item counts are better covered by component tests, while declared UI captures should target settled states with selectors that exist there. Also, rendering an outgoing skeleton beside a flex-growing route can change the route’s available space; when a cross-fade is not required, a direct conditional swap keeps layout behavior predictable.
